idiom_name: discriminated-union ControlCommand + exhaustive switch dispatch + node:diagnostics_channel
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds compile-time safety to the JavaScript realizations: the command vocabulary is a discriminated union (type ControlCommand = {op:'suspend', route:string, reason:string} | {op:'resume', route:string} | {op:'snapshot'}), the dispatcher is an exhaustive switch the compiler checks, and node:diagnostics_channel or the cluster/worker IPC carries the messages, with a thin admin endpoint exposing the same union to a console. The type system is the contract - a console compiled against the same union cannot send a command the component does not implement, which is what the classic pattern achieves with a message schema. Keep the schema-validated broker form when components are polyglot and the contract must be language-neutral.
pitfalls: Types vanish at runtime: a command arriving over IPC or HTTP is only as trustworthy as its validation, so narrow the payload with a schema (zod/io-ts) before dispatch or a malformed message reaches the switch.
Exhaustiveness only holds while the switch has no default clause; a default: return notImplemented silently re-opens the gap the union was meant to close.

Adding a command to the union breaks every consumer at compile time (the point of the design) but only if all consoles and services are built from the same published types package - a copied union drifts.

variants.name: Schema-validated control subjects (NATS) for polyglot deployments
variants.idiom_name: zod-validated ControlCommand on control.<component>.cmd with correlated reply subject
variants.implementation_notes: In a polyglot deployment the control contract cannot be a TypeScript union, so it is published as a schema (JSON Schema, Protobuf or Avro) and the TypeScript types are generated from - or validated against - it; components subscribe to control.<component>.cmd through the broker client, validate the decoded payload, and answer on the correlated reply subject or inbox. This keeps the control bus language-neutral: the same bytes mean the same command to a TypeScript service, a Go consumer or a Java route. Choose it when the console or the components are not all TypeScript; otherwise the typed in-process channel is cheaper.
pitfalls: Schemas drift from the published contract unless the schema is the source of truth in CI and the types are generated from it; an unvalidated 'typed' payload is worse than an untyped one because it looks checked.
Replies must be correlated (explicit correlation id or the broker's reply inbox) or acknowledgements from concurrent commands interleave and the console applies the wrong status.

Subject ownership is not enforced by the client library: a component subscribing to a wildcard control subject will execute commands aimed at other services unless the broker's permissions restrict it.
